project.name: LeadFlow
project.one_liner: Lead management app for a sales team that lives in it all day.

decisions.title: Desktop-first workspace
decisions.value: Design for desktop first; mobile is a deliberate adaptation for quick actions.
decisions.rationale: Reps work at a desk all day.

decisions.title: Persistent sidebar navigation
decisions.value: Left sidebar always visible on desktop; collapses to icons under 1200px.
decisions.rationale: Daily use across several top-level areas.

decisions.title: Medium-high information density
decisions.value: Compact rows and tight spacing; comfortable line height for scanning.

decisions.title: Lead detail drawer
decisions.value: Selecting a lead opens a side drawer so the list keeps its place.

decisions.title: Table-first lead management
decisions.value: Leads live in a sortable, filterable table with saved views.

decisions.title: Mobile experience
decisions.rationale: Decides which screens get a real mobile layout.

options.label: Quick actions
options.hint: Reply, update status, log a call

decisions.question: How should mobile users primarily use LeadFlow?

decisions.title: Primary user: sales reps
decisions.value: Sales representatives following up their own leads, plus a manager reviewing pipeline.

decisions.title: Core job: follow up leads
decisions.value: Know who to contact next and log what happened in seconds.

decisions.title: Fast repeated actions
decisions.value: Inline editing, keyboard shortcuts and a command palette for search and actions.

decisions.title: Undo over confirmation
decisions.value: Prefer undo toasts to confirmation dialogs; confirm only bulk deletes.

decisions.title: Responsive web application
decisions.value: Single web app that adapts across screen sizes; no native app in v1.

decisions.title: Dashboard structure
decisions.rationale: Sets what people see first each morning.
decisions.question: What should the home screen lead with?

decisions.title: WCAG 2.2 AA baseline
decisions.value: Full keyboard operation, visible focus, 4.5:1 text contrast, labelled controls.

decisions.title: Empty, loading and error states
decisions.value: Skeleton loaders, actionable empty states and plain-language errors with a retry.

decisions.title: Light-first theme
decisions.value: Light theme by default; tokens support dark later.

decisions.title: Slow-network tolerance
decisions.value: Lean payloads, skeletons and retryable requests for patchy connections.

decisions.title: Constraint
decisions.value: Reps lose leads because follow-ups live in personal spreadsheets and nobody can see what is overdue.

decisions.title: The bet
decisions.value: Reps adopt a shared list if it is faster than their spreadsheet; about three weeks; watch contact within 48 hours.

directions.name: Operational Precision
directions.fit: Built for people who repeat the same actions all day. Nothing decorative gets between a rep and the next lead.
directions.tradeoffs: Less visual personality; needs disciplined spacing to stay calm at high density.

directions.name: Modern CRM
directions.fit: Friendlier and easier to learn, suited to occasional users or teams new to CRM tools.
directions.tradeoffs: Fewer rows per screen; heavy users will scroll more.

directions.name: Command Center
directions.fit: Best when managers watch the pipeline live and reps work from queues and alerts.
directions.tradeoffs: Dark and dense can feel heavy; more effort to keep accessible.

risks.text: High density can hurt new starters; onboarding hints may be needed.
Mobile scope is undecided until PG-006 is answered.

assumptions.text: Fewer than 50 concurrent users, so no virtualisation needed for tables in v1.

constraint.statement: Reps lose leads because follow-ups live in personal spreadsheets and nobody can see what is overdue.
constraint.evidence: Last quarter's pipeline review found 31 leads with no contact for over 14 days.

forces.push: Missed follow-ups and no shared view of the pipeline.
forces.pull: One list that shows who to call today.
forces.anxiety: Reps worry the tool will slow them down or be used to monitor them.
forces.habit: Each rep keeps a private spreadsheet.

existing_assets: Current lead export from the website form

bet.belief: reps will adopt a shared list if it is faster than their spreadsheet
bet.wager: about three weeks of build effort
bet.expected_outcome: fewer leads going cold and a shared view of overdue follow-ups
bet.leading_indicator: share of leads contacted within 48 hours

outcomes: Overdue follow-ups are visible to the whole team
